short: turning a value of one type into another, written CAST(x AS t) or x::t. a cast from text is a parse and can fail.
a cast pg_cast lets postgres add on its own, anywhere it helps, like integer to bigint. assignment casts only happen when storing into a column.
a quoted string with no type yet. it takes the type the operator or column next to it wants, which is why '1' + 1 is 2.
exact decimal arithmetic at any size, numeric(p, s) to fix the scale. slower and bigger than integers or floats, right for money.
double precision: an IEEE 754 binary float, fast and approximate. it can't hold 0.1 exactly, so never compare it with =.
the rules a database uses to order and compare text. C is byte order; ICU collations sort like a dictionary in a given language.
an ICU collation that can call different strings equal, like Zoë and ZOË under und-u-ks-level2. postgres's way to compare without case.
a span of time stored as three separate counts: months, days and microseconds. + 1 month clamps to the month's end.
timestamp with time zone: an instant, stored as UTC, read and printed in the session's TimeZone. it stores no zone.
a type whose values are a fixed list of labels, sorted in the order they were declared. you can add labels but never drop one.
an existing type with constraints attached under a new name, checked whenever a value becomes that type.
a column numbered by its own sequence: GENERATED ALWAYS (or BY DEFAULT) AS IDENTITY. the standard form of serial.
a uuid whose first 48 bits are unix milliseconds, so new values sort last. postgres 18 generates them with uuidv7().
a typed list in one column, like text[]. subscripts start at 1; = ANY, @>, && and unnest work with it.
json parsed into a binary form: keys sorted and deduplicated, indexable with GIN. json keeps the original text instead.
a small query language for json values, used by @?, @@ and the jsonb_path_* functions.
turns a json document into rows and typed columns using paths. postgres 17 and later.
a start and an end as one value, each bound inclusive or exclusive: int4range, daterange, tstzrange. && asks whether two overlap.
an ordered set of non-overlapping ranges in one value, like {[1,3),[5,8)}. postgres 14 and later; range_agg builds one.
a read-only column computed from its own row. STORED keeps the value on disk; VIRTUAL, the default since 18, computes it on read.
